ma_willard_s_woods.blurb: A tiny bouldering stop inside a conservation area of about 100 acres in Lexington, north-west of Boston. Climbing is confined to one good-sized boulder, so treat it as a short session rather than a trip. The eleven problems start at the easiest grades and top out around V3, with most of them sitting near V2. Bring a crash pad. The boulder sits back in a more wooded stretch, while the rest of the property offers mowed meadows, pine groves, streams and a few miles of walking trails, which makes it a handy add-on to a family walk.

ma_shining_rock.blurb: A young, still-developing crag in Northbridge, in Worcester County, built around a large slab with a shorter, steeper face next to it. Eleven climbs mix a few boulder problems, some top-ropes, a pair of sport routes and a single trad line. The boulder problems are easy to moderate, up to about V3, and the roped climbs run from low fifth class up to a few stiffer lines near 5.12. It suits easy top-roping and moderate sport climbing more than hard projects. Expect graffiti on the rock and ongoing volunteer trail work.

ma_a_wall_aka_a_face.blurb: South of Boston at Quincy Quarries, this top-rope face is at the south end of the Little Railroad Quarry, one of the old cut walls. Ten of the eleven routes are top-ropes and one is trad. Grades start near 5.2, cluster between 5.4 and 5.9, and top out with a single 5.10. Drill holes left by the quarrymen mark the granite, and the wall is visited far less than its busier neighbours, so it works for beginners and for anyone wanting a quieter rope. A walk-off is available down the left side.
